source.text: וַיִּקְבְּצ֧וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אֶת־כָּל־מַחֲנֵיהֶ֖ם אֲפֵ֑קָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל חֹנִ֔ים בַּעַ֖יִן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered [the] Philistines all their camps to Aphek, and Israel [were] encamping at the spring which [is] in Jezreel.

en.L: And the Philistines gathered all their camps to Aphek, and Israel was encamped by the spring that is in Jezreel.
en.B: The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, while Israel was camped by the spring in Jezreel.
en.R: The Philistines brought all their armies together at Aphek. The Israelites were camped by the spring in the valley of Jezreel.

es.L: Y reunieron los filisteos todos sus campamentos en Afec, e Israel acampaba junto a la fuente que [está] en Jezreel.
es.B: Los filisteos reunieron todas sus fuerzas en Afec, mientras Israel acampaba junto a la fuente de Jezreel.
es.R: Los filisteos juntaron todos sus ejércitos en Afec. Los israelitas acampaban junto a la fuente que hay en el valle de Jezreel.

fr.L: Et les Philistins rassemblèrent tous leurs camps à Aphek, et Israël campait près de la source qui est à Jizreël.
fr.B: Les Philistins rassemblèrent toutes leurs forces à Aphek, tandis qu’Israël campait près de la source de Jizreël.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont rassemblé toutes leurs armées à Aphek. Les Israélites, eux, campaient près de la source, dans la vallée de Jizreël.

sw.L: Wafilisti wakakusanya kambi zao zote Afeki, naye Israeli alikuwa amepiga kambi karibu na chemchemi iliyoko Yezreeli.
sw.B: Wafilisti wakakusanya majeshi yao yote huko Afeki, nao Israeli walikuwa wamepiga kambi karibu na chemchemi iliyoko Yezreeli.
sw.R: Wafilisti wakakusanya majeshi yao yote huko Afeki. Waisraeli walikuwa wamepiga kambi karibu na chemchemi katika bonde la Yezreeli.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin tập hợp tất cả các trại quân của họ tại A-phéc, còn Y-sơ-ra-ên đóng trại bên dòng suối ở Gít-rê-ên.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin tập trung toàn bộ quân lực tại A-phéc, còn Y-sơ-ra-ên đóng trại bên dòng suối ở Gít-rê-ên.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin tập hợp tất cả quân đội tại A-phéc. Người Y-sơ-ra-ên đóng trại bên dòng suối trong thung lũng Gít-rê-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 사람들이 그들의 모든 진영을 아벡에 모았고, 이스라엘은 이스르엘에 있는 샘 곁에 진을 치고 있었다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들은 모든 군대를 아벡에 모았고, 이스라엘은 이스르엘에 있는 샘 곁에 진을 치고 있었다.
ko.R: 블레셋 사람들은 모든 군대를 아벡에 모았다. 이스라엘 사람들은 이스르엘 골짜기에 있는 샘 곁에 진을 쳤다.

decisions.choice: the Philistines gathered: the story returns to 28:1-2
decisions.reason: Chapter 28 began with the Philistines gathering for war and Achish taking David with him (28:1-2). The account then turned to Saul at Endor (28:3-25). This verse picks up the Philistine march again, at an earlier point: the armies are still assembling at Aphek, before they reach Shunem and Jezreel (28:4; verse 11).

decisions.choice: Aphek and Jezreel: the Philistine gathering place and the Israelite camp
decisions.reason: This Aphek lies on the coastal plain, where the Philistine armies had gathered before (4:1). From there they marched north to the valley of Jezreel, where Israel camped by a spring below Mount Gilboa, the place of the battle in chapter 31 (31:1).

decisions.choice: camps: armies, the fighting forces
decisions.reason: The word means a camp, and also the troops that make up a camp. Here it is all the Philistine forces, each city's army with its own camp.

decisions.choice: The Israelites; the valley of Jezreel
decisions.reason: Readable names the people rather than the land, and says that Jezreel here is the valley, so that it is clear where the armies faced each other.

decisions.choice: "A-phéc"; "Gít-rê-ên"
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note's table, in the usual Protestant forms; "Gít-rê-ên" as for Ahinoam's town (25:43).

decisions.choice: "아벡"; "이스르엘"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms; this Jezreel is the valley in the north, not the town of 25:43, and Readable says so as the English does.

source.text: וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ עֹֽבְרִ֔ים לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִ֑ים וְדָוִ֣ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו עֹֽבְרִ֛ים בָּאַחֲרֹנָ֖ה עִם־אָכִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rulers of [the] Philistines [were] passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men [were] passing on in the rear with Achish.

en.L: And the rulers of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were passing on at the rear with Achish.
en.B: As the rulers of the Philistines marched past with their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men were marching at the rear with Achish.
en.R: The Philistine rulers marched past with their troops in groups of a hundred and a thousand. David and his men marched at the back with Achish.

es.L: Y los jefes de los filisteos pasaban por centenas y por millares, y David y sus hombres pasaban en la retaguardia con Aquis.
es.B: Mientras los jefes de los filisteos desfilaban con sus unidades de cien y de mil hombres, David y sus hombres marchaban en la retaguardia con Aquis.
es.R: Los jefes filisteos pasaban con sus tropas en grupos de cien y de mil. David y sus hombres marchaban atrás, con Aquis.

fr.L: Et les princes des Philistins défilaient par centaines et par milliers, et David et ses hommes défilaient à l’arrière avec Akish.
fr.B: Tandis que les princes des Philistins défilaient avec leurs unités de cent et de mille hommes, David et ses hommes marchaient à l’arrière avec Akish.
fr.R: Les princes philistins sont passés avec leurs soldats, en groupes de cent et de mille. David et ses hommes marchaient derrière, avec Akish.

sw.L: Wakuu wa Wafilisti walikuwa wakipita kwa mamia na kwa maelfu, naye Daudi na watu wake walikuwa wakipita nyuma pamoja na Akishi.
sw.B: Wakuu wa Wafilisti walipokuwa wakipita na vikosi vyao vya mamia na maelfu, Daudi na watu wake walikuwa wakitembea nyuma pamoja na Akishi.
sw.R: Wakuu wa Wafilisti wakapita pamoja na askari wao katika vikundi vya mia moja na vya elfu moja. Daudi na watu wake walitembea nyuma pamoja na Akishi.

vi.L: Các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đi qua từng trăm, từng ngàn, còn Đa-vít và những người của ông đi sau cùng với A-kích.
vi.B: Khi các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin dẫn các đơn vị trăm người và ngàn người diễu qua, thì Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đi ở hậu quân với A-kích.
vi.R: Các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin diễu hành qua với quân lính của họ, từng đội trăm người và ngàn người. Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đi ở phía sau với A-kích.

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 통치자들은 백 명씩, 천 명씩 지나가고 있었고, 다윗과 그의 부하들은 아기스와 함께 맨 뒤에서 지나가고 있었다.
ko.B: 블레셋 통치자들이 백 명 단위, 천 명 단위의 부대를 이끌고 지나가는 동안, 다윗과 그의 부하들은 아기스와 함께 맨 뒤에서 행진하고 있었다.
ko.R: 블레셋 통치자들이 군인들을 백 명씩, 천 명씩 무리 지어 이끌고 지나갔다. 다윗과 그의 부하들은 아기스와 함께 맨 뒤에서 행진했다.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This is the title of the rulers of the five Philistine cities, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (6:17-18). Achish is one of them, the king of Gath (27:2).

decisions.choice: passing on by hundreds and by thousands: marching past in their army units
decisions.reason: Each ruler leads his troops in units of a hundred and a thousand as they pass by, perhaps in review before the battle. This is how the commanders see David's band among them.

decisions.choice: in the rear with Achish: as Achish's own guard
decisions.reason: Achish had made David his bodyguard for life (28:2), so David and his men march with the king of Gath at the back of the column.

decisions.choice: with their units (Balanced); with their troops in groups (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "by hundreds and by thousands". Balanced and Readable say that these are the units of soldiers each ruler leads.

decisions.choice: les princes des Philistins
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for the rulers of the five cities (m1); "princes" keeps them apart from the army's "chefs" in verse 3.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los filisteos (rulers); los comandantes de los filisteos (commanders, verses 3-4, 9)
decisions.reason: The rulers of the five Philistine cities (m1) take the Samuel terms note's “los jefes de los filisteos”; the army's commanders (sarim) in this chapter are “los comandantes”, so the two groups stay apart, as the Hebrew keeps them.

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa Wafilisti"
decisions.reason: As the terms note: the rulers of the five Philistine cities are "wakuu wa Wafilisti" at every level; their army commanders (verses 3-4, 9) are "majemadari" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for the lords of the five Philistine cities (m1).

decisions.choice: "블레셋 통치자들" for the rulers of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set: the lords of the five Philistine cities (meaning decision m1).

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מָ֖ה הָעִבְרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל־שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים הֲלֽוֹא־זֶ֨ה דָוִ֜ד עֶ֣בֶד׀שָׁא֣וּל מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה אִתִּי֙ זֶ֤ה יָמִים֙ אוֹ־זֶ֣ה שָׁנִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־מָצָ֤אתִי בוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה מִיּ֥וֹם נָפְל֖וֹ עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] commanders of [the] Philistines, What [are] the Hebrews the these? And said Achish to [the] commanders of [the] Philistines, [Is] not this David, servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me this days or this years, and not I have found in him anything from [the] day of his falling until the day the this.

en.L: And the commanders of the Philistines said, "What are these Hebrews?" And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days or these years? And I have not found anything in him from the day he fell [to me] until this day."
en.B: The Philistine commanders asked, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" Achish answered the commanders of the Philistines, "Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with me for some time now, a year or more, and from the day he came over to me until today I have found no fault in him."
en.R: The Philistine commanders asked, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" Achish answered them, "This is David. He used to serve Saul, the king of Israel. He has been with me for more than a year. Ever since he came over to my side, I have not found anything wrong with him."

es.L: Y dijeron los comandantes de los filisteos: «¿Qué [hacen] estos hebreos?». Y dijo Aquis a los comandantes de los filisteos: «¿No es este David, siervo de Saúl rey de Israel, que ha estado conmigo estos días o estos años? Y no he hallado nada en él desde el día en que se pasó [a mí] hasta este día».
es.B: Los comandantes filisteos preguntaron: «¿Qué hacen aquí estos hebreos?». Aquis les respondió a los comandantes de los filisteos: «¿No es este David, el siervo de Saúl, rey de Israel? Ya hace tiempo que está conmigo, un año o más, y desde el día en que se pasó a mi lado hasta hoy no le he encontrado ninguna falta».
es.R: Los comandantes filisteos preguntaron: «¿Qué hacen aquí estos hebreos?». Aquis les contestó: «Este es David. Antes servía a Saúl, el rey de Israel. Ya lleva más de un año conmigo. Desde el día en que se pasó a mi lado, no le he encontrado nada malo».

fr.L: Et les chefs des Philistins dirent : « Que [font] ces Hébreux ? » Et Akish dit aux chefs des Philistins : « N’est-ce pas David, le serviteur de Saül, roi d’Israël, qui est avec moi depuis des jours ou des années ? Et je n’ai rien trouvé en lui depuis le jour où il est passé [chez moi] jusqu’à ce jour. »
fr.B: Les chefs des Philistins demandèrent : « Que font ici ces Hébreux ? » Akish répondit aux chefs des Philistins : « N’est-ce pas David, le serviteur de Saül, roi d’Israël ? Il est avec moi depuis un bon moment, un an ou plus, et depuis le jour où il est passé de mon côté jusqu’à aujourd’hui, je n’ai rien eu à lui reprocher. »
fr.R: Les chefs philistins ont demandé : « Qu’est-ce que ces Hébreux font ici ? » Akish leur a répondu : « C’est David. Il était au service de Saül, le roi d’Israël. Il est avec moi depuis plus d’un an. Depuis qu’il est passé de mon côté, je n’ai rien trouvé de mal en lui. »

sw.L: Majemadari wa Wafilisti wakasema, "Hawa Waebrania ni nini?" Akishi akawaambia majemadari wa Wafilisti, "Je, huyu si Daudi, mtumishi wa Sauli mfalme wa Israeli, aliyekuwa pamoja nami siku hizi au miaka hii? Wala sijaona neno lolote ndani yake tangu siku alipoangukia [kwangu] mpaka siku hii ya leo."
sw.B: Majemadari wa Wafilisti wakauliza, "Waebrania hawa wanafanya nini hapa?" Akishi akawajibu majemadari wa Wafilisti, "Je, huyu si Daudi, mtumishi wa Sauli mfalme wa Israeli? Amekuwa pamoja nami kwa muda sasa, mwaka mmoja au zaidi, na tangu siku alipohamia kwangu mpaka leo sijaona kosa lolote kwake."
sw.R: Majemadari wa Wafilisti wakauliza, "Waebrania hawa wanafanya nini hapa?" Akishi akawajibu, "Huyu ni Daudi. Zamani alikuwa akimtumikia Sauli, mfalme wa Israeli. Amekuwa pamoja nami kwa zaidi ya mwaka mmoja. Tangu alipohamia upande wangu, sijaona kosa lolote kwake."

vi.L: Các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin nói: "Những người Hê-bơ-rơ này là gì?" A-kích nói với các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin: "Đây chẳng phải là Đa-vít, đầy tớ của Sau-lơ vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, người đã ở với ta những ngày này hay những năm này sao? Từ ngày hắn ngả về [ta] cho đến ngày nay, ta không thấy gì nơi hắn cả."
vi.B: Các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin hỏi: "Những người Hê-bơ-rơ này làm gì ở đây?" A-kích trả lời các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin: "Đây chẳng phải là Đa-vít, đầy tớ của Sau-lơ vua Y-sơ-ra-ên sao? Hắn đã ở với ta một thời gian, một năm hay hơn, và từ ngày hắn sang với ta cho đến nay, ta không thấy lỗi gì nơi hắn."
vi.R: Các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin hỏi: "Những người Hê-bơ-rơ này làm gì ở đây?" A-kích trả lời: "Đây là Đa-vít. Hắn từng phục vụ Sau-lơ, vua Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hắn đã ở với ta hơn một năm nay. Từ ngày hắn sang phe ta, ta không thấy hắn làm điều gì sai trái cả."

ko.L: 그리고 블레셋 지휘관들이 말했다. "이 히브리 사람들은 무엇이냐?" 그러자 아기스가 블레셋 지휘관들에게 말했다. "이 사람은 이스라엘 왕 사울의 신하 다윗이 아니오? 그는 이 몇 날, 아니 몇 해를 나와 함께 있었는데, 그가 [나에게] 넘어온 날부터 오늘까지 나는 그에게서 아무것도 찾지 못했소."
ko.B: 블레셋 지휘관들이 물었다. "이 히브리 사람들은 여기서 무엇을 하는 것입니까?" 아기스가 블레셋 지휘관들에게 대답했다. "이 사람은 이스라엘 왕 사울의 신하였던 다윗이 아니오? 그는 벌써 일 년이 넘도록 나와 함께 있었소. 그가 내게로 넘어온 날부터 오늘까지 나는 그에게서 아무 허물도 찾지 못했소."
ko.R: 블레셋 지휘관들이 물었다. "이 히브리 사람들이 여기서 무엇을 하는 것입니까?" 아기스가 대답했다. "이 사람은 다윗이오. 그는 전에 이스라엘 왕 사울을 섬겼소. 그는 일 년 넘게 나와 함께 지냈소. 그가 내 편으로 넘어온 날부터 지금까지 나는 그에게서 아무 잘못도 찾지 못했소."

decisions.choice: commanders of the Philistines: the army's officers
decisions.reason: These are the military commanders, a different word from the "rulers" of the five cities in verse 2. In verse 6 Achish says it is the rulers who do not approve of David; the commanders speak for them.

decisions.choice: Hebrews: the name others used for Israelites
decisions.reason: Foreigners, and Philistines above all, call Israelites "Hebrews" (4:6; 13:19; 14:11). The question is scornful: what are these men doing in a Philistine army?

decisions.choice: these days or these years: for a long time now
decisions.reason: The phrase means a good while, perhaps more than a year. By the end of his stay David had lived in Philistine country a year and four months (27:7).

decisions.choice: the day he fell: the day he deserted to me
decisions.reason: To "fall" to someone means to go over to his side, to desert (2 Kings 25:11; Jeremiah 37:13-14). Achish counts David as a deserter from Saul whom he can trust (27:12).

decisions.choice: the servant of Saul (Literal, Balanced); used to serve Saul (Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the word means a king's officer, not a slave, so "servant" is used at every level, as for other officials of a king. Readable says it as an action, which makes plain that David no longer serves Saul.

decisions.choice: "majemadari wa Wafilisti"; "Waebrania"
decisions.reason: The army's officers (m1), a different word from the rulers of verse 2; "Waebrania" is the name foreigners give to Israelites (m2).

decisions.choice: "người Hê-bơ-rơ"; Achish speaks of David as "hắn" to the commanders, and they and he say "ông" / "vua" and "chúng tôi" / "ta"
decisions.reason: "Hebrews" is the name others used for Israelites (m2), as "Hê-bơ-rơ" in the Vietnamese New Testament; a king speaking of a vassal to his officers.

decisions.choice: the Philistine commanders speak to Achish in the formal polite style (L: plain question among themselves); Achish answers his fellow leaders in 하오체 ("아니오?", "찾지 못했소")
decisions.reason: Achish is a king, but these commanders are not his subjects and overrule him; Korean marks speech between men of rank with 하오체. "히브리 사람들" is the name others used for Israelites (meaning decision m2).

source.text: וַיִּקְצְפ֨וּ עָלָ֜יו שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לוֹ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים הָשֵׁ֣ב אֶת־הָאִ֗ישׁ וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל־מְקוֹמוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִפְקַדְתּ֣וֹ שָׁ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יֵרֵ֤ד עִמָּ֨נוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹא־יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֥נוּ לְשָׂטָ֖ן בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וּבַמֶּ֗ה יִתְרַצֶּ֥ה זֶה֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֲל֕וֹא בְּרָאשֵׁ֖י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָהֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And were angry with him [the] commanders of [the] Philistines, and said to him [the] commanders of [the] Philistines, Send back the man, and let him return to his place where you assigned him there, and not he shall go down with us into the battle, and not he shall become to us as an adversary in the battle; and with what will make himself acceptable this one to his lord? [Is it] not with [the] heads of the men the those?

en.L: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, "Send the man back, and let him return to his place where you assigned him, and he shall not go down with us into the battle, so that he does not become an adversary to us in the battle. And with what would this one make himself acceptable to his lord? Is it not with the heads of those men?
en.B: But the Philistine commanders were angry with Achish and said to him, "Send the man back! Let him go back to the place where you stationed him. He is not to go down to battle with us, or he may turn against us once the fighting starts. How could this fellow win back his master's favor? Surely with the heads of the men here!
en.R: But the Philistine commanders were angry with Achish. They said, "Send this man back to the town you gave him. He must not go into battle with us. Once the fighting starts, he could turn against us. Is there a better way for him to get back into his master's good graces? He could kill our men and take their heads to him!

es.L: Pero los comandantes de los filisteos se enojaron contra él, y le dijeron los comandantes de los filisteos: «Despide a este hombre, y que vuelva a su lugar donde lo pusiste, y que no baje con nosotros a la batalla, para que no se nos vuelva adversario en la batalla. ¿Pues con qué se haría este grato a su señor? ¿No [sería] con las cabezas de estos hombres?
es.B: Pero los comandantes filisteos se enojaron con Aquis y le dijeron: «¡Despide a ese hombre! Que vuelva al lugar donde lo estableciste. No debe bajar con nosotros a la batalla, no sea que se vuelva contra nosotros en medio del combate. ¿Cómo podría este tipo recobrar el favor de su señor? ¡Pues con las cabezas de nuestros hombres!
es.R: Pero los comandantes filisteos se enojaron con Aquis. Le dijeron: «Manda a este hombre de vuelta al pueblo que le diste. No debe ir a la batalla con nosotros. Cuando comience la pelea, podría ponerse en contra nuestra. ¿Qué mejor manera tendría de volver a ganarse a su señor? ¡Podría matar a nuestros hombres y llevarle sus cabezas!

fr.L: Mais les chefs des Philistins s’irritèrent contre lui, et les chefs des Philistins lui dirent : « Renvoie cet homme, et qu’il retourne à l’endroit où tu l’as établi ; et qu’il ne descende pas avec nous au combat, pour qu’il ne devienne pas pour nous un adversaire dans le combat. Et avec quoi celui-ci se rendrait-il agréable à son seigneur ? N’est-ce pas avec les têtes de ces hommes-là ?
fr.B: Mais les chefs des Philistins s’irritèrent contre Akish et lui dirent : « Renvoie cet homme ! Qu’il retourne à l’endroit où tu l’as installé. Il ne descendra pas au combat avec nous, de peur qu’il ne se retourne contre nous pendant la bataille. Comment ce gaillard pourrait-il regagner la faveur de son maître ? Avec les têtes de nos hommes, bien sûr !
fr.R: Mais les chefs philistins se sont mis en colère contre Akish. Ils lui ont dit : « Renvoie cet homme dans la ville que tu lui as donnée. Il ne doit pas venir au combat avec nous. Une fois la bataille commencée, il pourrait se retourner contre nous. Quel meilleur moyen aurait-il de se réconcilier avec son maître ? Il pourrait tuer nos hommes et lui apporter leurs têtes !

sw.L: Lakini majemadari wa Wafilisti wakamkasirikia, nao majemadari wa Wafilisti wakamwambia, "Mrudishe mtu huyu, arudi mahali pake ulipomweka, wala asishuke pamoja nasi vitani, asije akawa adui yetu vitani. Kwa maana huyu angejipatanisha na bwana wake kwa kitu gani? Je, si kwa vichwa vya watu hawa?
sw.B: Lakini majemadari wa Wafilisti wakamkasirikia Akishi, wakamwambia, "Mrudishe mtu huyu! Arudi mahali ulipomweka. Asishuke pamoja nasi vitani, la sivyo atatugeuka vita vikianza. Mtu huyu angewezaje kupata tena kibali cha bwana wake? Hakika ni kwa vichwa vya watu walio hapa!
sw.R: Lakini majemadari wa Wafilisti wakamkasirikia Akishi. Wakasema, "Mrudishe mtu huyu katika mji uliompa. Asiende vitani pamoja nasi. Vita vikianza, anaweza kutugeuka. Je, kuna njia bora zaidi ya kujipatanisha na bwana wake? Angeweza kuwaua watu wetu na kumpelekea vichwa vyao!

vi.L: Nhưng các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin giận A-kích, và các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin nói với vua: "Xin vua cho người này trở về, để hắn về chỗ vua đã chỉ định cho hắn; hắn không được đi xuống chiến trận với chúng tôi, kẻo trong trận hắn trở thành kẻ địch của chúng tôi. Vì hắn lấy gì để làm cho chủ hắn hài lòng? Chẳng phải bằng đầu của những người này sao?
vi.B: Nhưng các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin giận A-kích và nói với vua: "Xin vua cho người này trở về! Hãy để hắn về nơi vua đã cho hắn ở. Hắn không được xuống trận với chúng tôi, kẻo khi giao chiến hắn lại trở mặt chống chúng tôi. Hắn lấy gì để lấy lại lòng chủ hắn? Chắc chắn là bằng đầu của những người lính ở đây!
vi.R: Nhưng các tướng lĩnh Phi-li-tin giận A-kích. Họ nói: "Xin vua cho người này trở về thành vua đã ban cho hắn. Hắn không được ra trận với chúng tôi. Khi giao chiến, hắn có thể quay lại đánh chúng tôi. Hắn còn cách nào tốt hơn để lấy lòng chủ hắn? Hắn có thể giết người của chúng ta và đem đầu họ về cho chủ hắn!

ko.L: 그러나 블레셋 지휘관들이 그에게 화를 냈다. 그리고 블레셋 지휘관들이 그에게 말했다. "그 사람을 돌려보내어, 당신이 그를 둔 그의 곳으로 돌아가게 하십시오. 그가 우리와 함께 싸움에 내려가지 않게 하여, 그가 싸움터에서 우리의 대적이 되지 않게 하십시오. 이 자가 무엇으로 자기 주인의 마음을 얻겠습니까? 이 사람들의 머리로 하지 않겠습니까?
ko.B: 그러나 블레셋 지휘관들은 아기스에게 화를 내며 말했다. "그 사람을 돌려보내십시오! 당신이 그에게 정해 준 곳으로 돌아가게 하십시오. 그가 우리와 함께 싸움터에 내려가서는 안 됩니다. 싸움이 시작되면 그가 우리를 칠지도 모릅니다. 이 자가 자기 주인의 마음을 다시 얻으려면 무엇이 더 좋겠습니까? 바로 여기 있는 우리 군사들의 머리가 아니겠습니까!
ko.R: 그러나 블레셋 지휘관들은 아기스에게 화를 냈다. 그들이 말했다. "이 사람을 당신이 준 마을로 돌려보내십시오. 그가 우리와 함께 싸우러 가서는 안 됩니다. 싸움이 시작되면 그가 우리에게 등을 돌릴 수도 있습니다. 그가 자기 주인의 마음을 다시 얻는 데 이보다 더 좋은 방법이 있겠습니까? 그는 우리 군사들을 죽여서 그 머리를 주인에게 가져갈 수도 있습니다!

decisions.choice: his place where you assigned him: the town of Ziklag
decisions.reason: Achish had given David the town of Ziklag to live in (27:5-6). The commanders want him sent back there, out of the battle.

decisions.choice: an adversary: an opponent who turns against us
decisions.reason: The word names anyone who opposes another, here a soldier who changes sides in the middle of the fight (compare 2 Samuel 19:23; 1 Kings 11:14). Elsewhere the same word becomes the name of the Accuser, Satan (Job 1:6), but here it is a human enemy.

decisions.choice: with what would he make himself acceptable to his lord: how better to win back Saul's favor
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer the commanders give: David could make peace with his master Saul by bringing him the heads of Philistine soldiers, as he once brought Goliath's (17:54, 57) and the foreskins of a hundred Philistines (18:27).

decisions.choice: those men: our own men
decisions.reason: "Those men" are the Philistine soldiers around them. The commanders may avoid saying "our men" as one avoids naming a harm one fears for oneself.

decisions.choice: angry with Achish
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "with him". Balanced and Readable name Achish so that the reader does not think the commanders were speaking to David.

decisions.choice: He could kill our men and take their heads to him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the question about "the heads of those men" implies and turns it into a plain statement.

source.text: הֲלוֹא־זֶ֣ה דָוִ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יַעֲנוּ־ל֛וֹ בַּמְּחֹל֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽאֲלָפָ֔יו וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not this David of whom they sing to one another in the dances, saying, Struck down Saul his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

en.L: Is this not David, of whom they sing to one another in the dances, saying, \q 'Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his ten thousands'?"
en.B: Is this not the David they sang about to one another as they danced, \q 'Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands'?"
en.R: This is the same David the women sang about as they danced. They sang, \q 'Saul has killed his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands.'"

es.L: ¿No es este David, de quien cantaban unas a otras en las danzas, diciendo: \q “Saúl ha abatido a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles”?».
es.B: ¿No es este el David de quien cantaban unas a otras mientras danzaban: \q “Saúl ha derribado a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles”?».
es.R: Este es el mismo David de quien cantaban las mujeres mientras bailaban. Cantaban: \q “Saúl ha matado a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles”».

fr.L: N’est-ce pas ce David dont on chantait en se répondant dans les danses, en disant : \q “Saül a frappé ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers” ? »
fr.B: N’est-ce pas ce David que l’on chantait en se répondant dans les danses : \q “Saül a frappé ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers” ? »
fr.R: C’est ce même David que les femmes chantaient en dansant. Elles chantaient : \q “Saül a tué ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers.” »

sw.L: Je, huyu si Daudi, ambaye wanamwimba wakijibizana katika ngoma, wakisema, \q 'Sauli amewapiga maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi elfu yake'?"
sw.B: Je, huyu si yule Daudi waliyemwimba wakijibizana walipokuwa wakicheza, \q 'Sauli amewapiga maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi ya maelfu yake'?"
sw.R: Huyu ndiye yule Daudi ambaye wanawake walimwimba walipokuwa wakicheza. Waliimba, \q 'Sauli ameua maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi ya maelfu yake.'"

vi.L: Đây chẳng phải là Đa-vít mà người ta đã hát đối đáp với nhau trong các điệu múa rằng: \q 'Sau-lơ đã đánh hạ hàng ngàn của mình, \q còn Đa-vít hàng vạn của mình' sao?"
vi.B: Đây chẳng phải là Đa-vít mà người ta đã hát đối đáp với nhau khi nhảy múa: \q 'Sau-lơ giết hàng ngàn, \q còn Đa-vít giết hàng vạn' sao?"
vi.R: Đây chính là Đa-vít mà các phụ nữ đã hát khi nhảy múa. Họ hát: \q 'Sau-lơ giết được hàng ngàn, \q còn Đa-vít giết được hàng vạn.'"

ko.L: 이 사람은 사람들이 춤추면서 서로 주고받으며 이렇게 노래한 다윗이 아닙니까? \q '사울은 수천을 쳐 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만을 [쳐 죽였다].'"
ko.B: 이 사람은 사람들이 춤추며 서로 주고받으며 노래한 바로 그 다윗이 아닙니까? \q '사울은 수천을 쳐 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만을 쳐 죽였다.'"
ko.R: 이 사람은 여자들이 춤추면서 노래한 바로 그 다윗입니다. 그들은 이렇게 노래했습니다. \q '사울은 수천 명을 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만 명을 죽였다.'"

decisions.choice: the women's song of 18:7
decisions.reason: This is the third time the song is quoted, in the same words as 18:7 and 21:12. Saul heard it as setting David above him (18:8); in Gath it had put David in danger (21:12-13); now it is the reason the Philistine commanders will not let him fight beside them.

decisions.choice: sing to one another: sang in turn, one group answering another
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "answer". Used of singing it means a song sung in parts, one group replying to another, as in 18:7.

decisions.choice: his thousands ... his ten thousands: the marginal spelling
decisions.reason: As in 21:12, the consonants written in the text spell the endings of these two words in a shorter way, and the reading noted by the scribes in the margin gives the usual plural form, as in 18:7. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the song in the same words as 18:7, set in two lines
decisions.reason: The song keeps the wording it has at each level in 18:7 and 21:12, so the reader hears the same lines each time. Readable turns the question into a statement and names the women who sang (18:6-7), since "they" alone would be unclear.

decisions.choice: the women's song as in 18:7 and 21:12
decisions.reason: The song keeps at each level the Swahili wording of 18:7 and 21:12.

decisions.choice: the women's song in the same Korean words as 18:7 and 21:12, set in two lines
decisions.reason: The song is quoted a third time (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps one wording at each level so the echo is heard.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לָיו חַי־יְהוָ֞ה כִּי־יָשָׁ֣ר אַתָּ֗ה וְט֣וֹב בְּ֠עֵינַי צֵאתְךָ֨וּבֹאֲךָ֤ אִתִּי֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא־מָצָ֤אתִֽי בְךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם בֹּאֲךָ֥ אֵלַ֖י עַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֥י הַסְּרָנִ֖ים לֹֽא־ט֥וֹב אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Achish to David and said to him, [By the] life [of] Yahweh, surely upright [are] you, and good in my eyes [is] your going out and your coming in with me in the camp, for not I have found in you evil from [the] day of your coming to me until the day the this; but in [the] eyes of the rulers not good [are] you.

en.L: And Achish called David and said to him, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you are upright, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp [is] good in my eyes, for I have not found evil in you from the day you came to me until this day. But in the eyes of the rulers you are not good.
en.B: So Achish called David and said to him, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you have been honest, and I would be glad to have you march out and come back with me in the army. I have found nothing wrong in you from the day you came to me until today. But the rulers do not approve of you.
en.R: So Achish called for David. He said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you have been loyal to me. I would be glad to have you go into battle with me in my army. Since the day you came to me, I have not found anything wrong with you. But the other rulers do not trust you.

es.L: Y llamó Aquis a David y le dijo: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que tú eres recto, y tu salir y tu entrar conmigo en el campamento [es] bueno a mis ojos, porque no he hallado mal en ti desde el día en que viniste a mí hasta este día. Pero a los ojos de los jefes no eres bueno.
es.B: Entonces Aquis llamó a David y le dijo: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, tú has sido honrado, y me agradaría que salieras y volvieras conmigo en el ejército. No he encontrado nada malo en ti desde el día en que llegaste a mí hasta hoy. Pero los jefes no te aprueban.
es.R: Entonces Aquis llamó a David. Le dijo: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, tú me has sido leal. Me gustaría que fueras conmigo a la batalla en mi ejército. Desde el día en que llegaste a mí, no te he encontrado nada malo. Pero los otros jefes no confían en ti.

fr.L: Et Akish appela David et lui dit : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, tu es droit, et ta sortie et ton entrée avec moi dans le camp [sont] bonnes à mes yeux, car je n’ai pas trouvé de mal en toi depuis le jour où tu es venu chez moi jusqu’à ce jour. Mais aux yeux des princes, tu n’es pas bon.
fr.B: Akish appela donc David et lui dit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, tu es un homme droit, et j’aurais aimé te voir partir et revenir avec moi dans l’armée. Je n’ai rien trouvé de mal en toi depuis le jour où tu es venu chez moi jusqu’à aujourd’hui. Mais les princes ne veulent pas de toi.
fr.R: Alors Akish a fait venir David. Il lui a dit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, tu as été loyal envers moi. J’aurais été content que tu partes au combat avec moi dans mon armée. Depuis le jour où tu es arrivé chez moi, je n’ai rien trouvé de mal en toi. Mais les autres princes n’ont pas confiance en toi.

sw.L: Akishi akamwita Daudi, akamwambia, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, wewe ni mnyofu, na kutoka kwako na kuingia kwako pamoja nami kambini [ni] vyema machoni pangu, kwa maana sijaona ubaya ndani yako tangu siku ulipokuja kwangu mpaka siku hii ya leo. Lakini machoni pa wakuu wewe si mwema.
sw.B: Basi Akishi akamwita Daudi, akamwambia, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, umekuwa mwaminifu, nami ningefurahi kutoka na kurudi pamoja nawe katika jeshi. Sijaona kosa lolote kwako tangu siku ulipokuja kwangu mpaka leo. Lakini wakuu hawakukubali.
sw.R: Basi Akishi akamwita Daudi. Akasema, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, umekuwa mwaminifu kwangu. Ningefurahi uende vitani pamoja nami katika jeshi langu. Tangu siku ulipokuja kwangu, sijaona kosa lolote kwako. Lakini wakuu wengine hawakuamini.

vi.L: A-kích gọi Đa-vít và nói với ông: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, ngươi là người ngay thẳng, và việc ngươi ra vào với ta trong trại quân [là] tốt trước mắt ta, vì từ ngày ngươi đến với ta cho đến ngày nay ta không thấy điều ác nơi ngươi. Nhưng trước mắt các lãnh chúa thì ngươi không tốt.
vi.B: Vậy A-kích gọi Đa-vít đến và nói với ông: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, ngươi là người ngay thẳng, và ta rất muốn ngươi cùng ta ra trận và trở về trong đạo quân. decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: a Philistine king swears by Israel's God
decisions.reason: Achish swears by the life of Yahweh, the strongest oath an Israelite could make (20:3). He may use David's own oath to assure him that he means what he says. The narrator does not explain it.

decisions.choice: upright: straight, honest and loyal
decisions.reason: The word describes someone straight in his dealings. Achish trusts David completely, though the reader knows David had deceived him about his raids (27:8-12).

decisions.choice: your going out and your coming in: taking part in the campaign
decisions.reason: Going out and coming in is a common way to speak of leading or serving in war (18:13, 16; 2 Samuel 3:25). Achish would gladly have David fight beside him.

decisions.choice: in the eyes of the rulers you are not good: the rulers do not approve of you
decisions.reason: "Good in someone's eyes" means approved or pleasing to him. Achish sets his own view against the other rulers': to him David is good; to them he is not.

decisions.choice: honest (Balanced); loyal, do not trust you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the Hebrew "upright" and "not good in their eyes" in everyday words. Readable adds "other" before rulers, since Achish is one of them.

decisions.choice: the oath "주께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데" in the mouth of a Philistine king
decisions.reason: A Philistine king swears by Israel's God (meaning decision m1); Korean keeps the same oath form, with the divine name span, as everywhere in the book.

decisions.choice: the enemies of my lord the king: words with a double edge
alternatives: my lord the king = Achish only
decisions.reason: On the surface David means Achish, and asks to fight Achish's enemies, the Israelites. But "my lord the king" is how David has spoken of Saul (24:9; 26:17), and the enemies of Saul would be the Philistines. The narrator leaves it open whom David truly means and what he would have done in the battle.

decisions.choice: from the day that I was before you: from the day I entered your service
decisions.reason: To "be before" a king is to stand in his presence as his servant (16:21-22).

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to a king, a subject calls himself "your servant" (17:32; 26:18).

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Readable says "me" for the polite "your servant", which is how a reader today would say it. It keeps "my lord the king" so that the double meaning stays.

decisions.choice: "các kẻ thù của bệ hạ" (B), "của đức vua" (R)
alternatives: "chúa tôi là vua" at every level
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "bệ hạ" and "đức vua" are the forms of "my lord the king" at these levels (terms note); they keep the double edge the meaning decision notes (m1), since the words never say which king.

decisions.choice: "내 주 임금님의 원수들" kept without saying which king
decisions.reason: David's words have a double edge (meaning decision m1): "my lord the king" could be Achish or Saul. Korean keeps the ambiguity by using the same title David uses for Saul.

decisions.choice: like an angel of God: wholly good and trustworthy
decisions.reason: To compare a man to an angel, a messenger from God, is high praise at a royal court: it says he is faultless and can be fully trusted. The same comparison is made of David later, for his wisdom and fairness as king (2 Samuel 14:17, 20; 19:28). On the lips of a Philistine the word for God could also be heard as "gods", making the phrase "a messenger of the gods", but Achish has just sworn by Yahweh (verse 6), so "God" fits his words here.

decisions.choice: nevertheless: yet, all the same
decisions.reason: The word sets Achish's own trust in David against the commanders' decision, which he cannot overrule.

decisions.choice: an angel of God (Literal, Balanced); an angel from God (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not mark the phrase as "the" angel, so "an angel" is used. Readable says "from God" to make plain that an angel is a messenger God sends.

decisions.choice: you are as good as an angel from God, as far as I am concerned
decisions.reason: Readable puts "in my eyes" at the end as "as far as I am concerned", so that the comparison comes first.

es.L: Ahora, pues, madruga por la mañana, [tú] y los siervos de tu señor que vinieron contigo; y {{plural_you:levántense|levantaos}} temprano por la mañana, y [cuando] {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} luz, {{plural_you:váyanse|idos}}».
es.B: Así que levántate temprano por la mañana, tú y los siervos de tu señor que vinieron contigo. {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} en camino temprano, y en cuanto haya luz, {{plural_you:váyanse|marchaos}}».
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:levántense|levantaos}} temprano por la mañana, tú y los hombres de tu señor que vinieron contigo. {{plural_you:Váyanse|Marchaos}} en cuanto haya luz».

fr.L: Et maintenant, lève-toi de bon matin, [toi] et les serviteurs de ton seigneur qui sont venus avec toi. Et levez-vous de bon matin, et [dès que] le jour vous éclairera, partez. »
fr.B: Lève-toi donc de bon matin, toi et les serviteurs de ton maître qui sont venus avec toi. Levez-vous de bon matin, et dès qu’il fera jour, partez. »
fr.R: Alors lève-toi tôt demain matin, toi et les hommes de ton maître qui sont venus avec toi. Partez dès qu’il fera jour. »

sw.L: Basi sasa, amka asubuhi na mapema, [wewe] na watumishi wa bwana wako waliokuja pamoja nawe. Mkiisha kuamka asubuhi na mapema, kukiwa kumekucha kwenu, nendeni."
sw.B: Basi amka asubuhi na mapema, wewe na watumishi wa bwana wako waliokuja pamoja nawe. Ondokeni asubuhi na mapema, na kukishapambazuka, nendeni zenu."
sw.R: Basi amkeni asubuhi na mapema, wewe na watu wa bwana wako waliokuja pamoja nawe. Ondokeni mara kukishapambazuka."

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, sáng sớm mai hãy dậy, [ngươi] và các đầy tớ của chủ ngươi đã đến với ngươi. Hãy dậy sớm vào buổi sáng, và [khi] trời sáng thì đi."
vi.B: Vậy sáng sớm mai, ngươi và các đầy tớ của chủ ngươi đã theo ngươi hãy dậy. Hãy dậy sớm, và trời vừa sáng thì đi."
vi.R: Vậy sáng mai hãy dậy sớm, ngươi và những người của chủ ngươi đã theo ngươi. Trời vừa sáng thì hãy đi."

ko.L: 그러니 이제 너와 너와 함께 온 네 주인의 종들은 아침에 일찍 일어나라. 아침에 일찍 일어나서 날이 밝으면 떠나라."
ko.B: 그러니 너와 너와 함께 온 네 주인의 신하들은 아침 일찍 일어나라. 아침 일찍 일어나서 날이 밝는 대로 떠나라."
ko.R: 그러니 너와 너와 함께 온 네 주인의 부하들은 아침 일찍 일어나서, 날이 밝으면 곧 떠나라."

decisions.choice: the servants of your lord: David's men, once subjects of Saul
decisions.reason: "Your lord" is most likely Saul. Achish describes David's men as Saul's subjects who came over to Gath with David, perhaps hinting why the commanders do not trust them. It could also be Achish's own polite way of speaking of himself, but nothing in the verse shows that.

decisions.choice: a shorter text
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has a longer verse here: Achish also tells David to go to the place he had assigned him and not to let any bad thought stay in his heart, because he is good in Achish's sight. The Hebrew text, followed here, does not have these words. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: rise early ... rise early: the order repeated
decisions.reason: Achish says twice that they must start early. The repetition presses the point: David and his men must be gone before the armies march.

decisions.choice: one command to get up early, then Leave as soon as it is light
decisions.reason: Readable gives the repeated order once, since it adds no new meaning, and keeps the time of leaving.

decisions.choice: your master's men
decisions.reason: Readable uses "men" for the servants, who are David's fighting men (verse 2), not household servants.

decisions.choice: singular, then plural commands to David and his men, with the plural_you span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from David alone to David and the servants of his lord (m1), and the later commands are plural; Spanish shows the plural with the plural_you span.

records.literal_gloss: And rose early David, he and his men, to go in the morning, to return to [the] land of [the] Philistines; and [the] Philistines went up [to] Jezreel.

en.L: And David rose early, he and his men, to go in the morning, to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up [to] Jezreel.
en.B: So David and his men got up early to set out in the morning and go back to the land of the Philistines, while the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
en.R: So David and his men got up early in the morning and set out to go back to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistine army went up to Jezreel.

es.L: Y madrugó David, él y sus hombres, para irse por la mañana, para volver a la tierra de los filisteos. Y los filisteos subieron [a] Jezreel.
es.B: Así que David y sus hombres se levantaron temprano para ponerse en camino por la mañana y volver a la tierra de los filisteos, mientras los filisteos subían a Jezreel.
es.R: Así que David y sus hombres se levantaron temprano por la mañana y se pusieron en camino para volver a la tierra de los filisteos. Y el ejército filisteo subió a Jezreel.

fr.L: Et David se leva de bon matin, lui et ses hommes, pour partir au matin, pour retourner au pays des Philistins. Et les Philistins montèrent à Jizreël.
fr.B: David et ses hommes se levèrent donc de bon matin pour partir et retourner au pays des Philistins, tandis que les Philistins montaient à Jizreël.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes se sont levés tôt le matin et ils sont partis pour retourner au pays des Philistins. Et l’armée philistine est montée à Jizreël.

sw.L: Daudi akaamka asubuhi na mapema, yeye na watu wake, ili kwenda asubuhi, kurudi katika nchi ya Wafilisti. Nao Wafilisti wakapanda [kwenda] Yezreeli.
sw.B: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaamka mapema ili kuondoka asubuhi na kurudi katika nchi ya Wafilisti, nao Wafilisti wakapanda kwenda Yezreeli.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaamka asubuhi na mapema, wakaondoka kurudi katika nchi ya Wafilisti. Nalo jeshi la Wafilisti likapanda kwenda Yezreeli.

vi.L: Đa-vít dậy sớm, ông và những người của ông, để ra đi vào buổi sáng, trở về xứ Phi-li-tin. Còn người Phi-li-tin đi lên Gít-rê-ên.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ dậy sớm để lên đường vào buổi sáng, trở về xứ Phi-li-tin, còn người Phi-li-tin thì đi lên Gít-rê-ên.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ dậy sớm vào buổi sáng và lên đường trở về xứ Phi-li-tin. Còn quân Phi-li-tin thì đi lên Gít-rê-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그와 그의 부하들과 함께 아침에 일찍 일어나 블레셋 사람들의 땅으로 돌아가려고 떠났다. 그리고 블레셋 사람들은 이스르엘로 올라갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하들은 아침 일찍 일어나 블레셋 땅으로 돌아가려고 길을 떠났고, 블레셋 사람들은 이스르엘로 올라갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하들은 아침 일찍 일어나 블레셋 사람들의 땅으로 돌아가려고 떠났다. 그리고 블레셋 군대는 이스르엘로 올라갔다.

decisions.choice: the Philistines went up to Jezreel: the two parties go opposite ways
decisions.reason: The verse sets David's return south against the Philistines' march north to fight Israel. David is kept out of the battle in which Saul dies (31:1-6), and he goes back to find Ziklag raided (30:1).

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines: back to Ziklag
decisions.reason: David returns to the town Achish gave him in Philistine territory (27:6; 30:1).

decisions.choice: the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" to show that it is the fighting force, not the whole people, that marches to Jezreel.
